definition: Incident identifier from incident-register.csv. Real incidents INC-001 upwards; INC-EXAMPLE-NN is reserved for fictional training rows and must say FICTIONAL in notes.
CONTROL: one row per causal factor and control (or per factor with control_id NONE). GATE: one row per incident and relevant critical gate.
Pseudonymous coder code. The key to names and the independence declarations is held by the study lead, not in this file. On RECONCILED rows, the adjudicator's code.
A and B are the two independent codings; RECONCILED is the agreed record after disagreement resolution. Agreement statistics use A and B only; metrics use RECONCILED only.
Y if the coder is not the framework author and has no design involvement in AIDCF; N otherwise.
Coder's familiarity with this incident's cause before coding, declared before reading the dossier.
allowed_values: NONE (no prior knowledge) | GENERAL (knew it happened, not the cause) | DETAILED (knew the cause or had read the report)

definition: Phase in which the causal factor was first identified. PRE_REVEAL: from the pre-event dossier before the analysis and remediation sections were read. POST_REVEAL: added after reading the full source. On GATE rows: the phase in which the gate was first judged relevant.
Semicolon-separated absolute URLs of every source used for this row, primary first.
Type of each URL in source_urls, in the same order. At least one PRIMARY or REGULATOR is required.
allowed_values: PRIMARY (the operator's or provider's own post-incident report) | REGULATOR (regulator, public inquiry or statutory investigation report) | SECONDARY_PRESS (reputable technical press)

definition: Date the coder last accessed the sources; must match an archived copy listed in the register.
Date of the initiating event as stated in the primary source (first day if multi-day).
Type of the operator or provider whose infrastructure failed.
allowed_values: AI_HPC_FACILITY | COLOCATION | ENTERPRISE | HYPERSCALE_CLOUD | MANAGED_SERVICE | OTHER | PUBLIC_SECTOR | TELECOM_NETWORK

definition: Primary sampling stratum: the infrastructure layer where the initiating failure occurred.
allowed_values: POWER | COOLING (including heat events and liquid cooling) | NETWORK_FABRIC | STORAGE | CONTROL_PLANE_OT | CHANGE_HUMAN | EXTERNAL_DEPENDENCY

definition: Neutral summary of the pre-event conditions and the observable outcome, written from the pre-event dossier before the root-cause and remediation sections are read. Paraphrase; no more than one short quotation.

Causal-factor identifier. Coding pass 1 (independent factor identification): CF-ANN or CF-BNN, local to the coder. Coding pass 2 and RECONCILED: consolidated CF-NN. GATE rows list the consolidated factors that engage the gate, semicolon-separated.
Position of the factor on the AIDCF-004 scenario path.
allowed_values: INITIATING (initiating event or condition) | PREDISPOSING (pre-existing condition increasing susceptibility) | ESCALATION (safeguard weakness that let the effect propagate or grow) | RECOVERY (condition that delayed or defeated recovery)

definition: The factor expressed as a condition that existed before the initiating event (a state, not the event). Must be traceable to a PRIMARY or REGULATOR source.
Whether the condition existed and could have been known before the event, on the source's own statements.
allowed_values: STATED_KNOWN (source states it was known or recorded before the event) | DISCOVERABLE (source states it existed before the event; it would be visible in records, configuration, test or inspection) | NOT_KNOWABLE (no reasonable pre-event record, test or inspection could have revealed it) | NOT_STATED (source does not say whether it existed before the event)

definition: AIDCF-004 failure-cause family, exactly as written in Part VI.
allowed_values: Design; Manufacturing; Installation; Commissioning; Configuration; Operation; Maintenance; Ageing; Capacity; Environment; Dependency; Control/monitoring; Human/organisational; Supplier/contract; Security; Change/transition; Recovery; UNKNOWN

definition: AIDCF-004 scenario family as DOMAIN:Family name, using the Part XIII name text before any dagger marker or parenthesis (for example THM:CDU failure; DEP:Hidden shared dependency). Semicolon-separated if more than one; the first is the primary family. List all valid codes with backtest_check.py --list-families.
Cross-domain library scenario(s) whose reference path the incident follows, or NONE.
Appendix A failure-mode IDs of the Required Functions that failed, semicolon-separated, or NONE if no catalogue row fits (then record a G6 gap).
Part VII mode codes. Must include the mode of every listed FM-* row. M00 if the manner is unresolved.
AIDCF-007A control whose objective or requirement addresses the factor. One control per row; NONE when no control addresses it. Pass 1 rows leave it empty.
Number(s) of the control's assessment criteria relied on for the judgement, from the AIDCF-007A control catalogue. Required for DETECTED, PARTIALLY_DETECTED and NOT_DETECTED.

Control result a competent assessor would have recorded at the reference date, applying the cited criteria with the evidence profile in registries/controls/evidence-profiles.csv. Required unless the judgement is NOT_ADDRESSED or INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION.

Would the control's assessment criteria and evidence profile have surfaced the condition before the event? Empty only when knowability is NOT_KNOWABLE. Full definitions and decision order in protocol section 10.
Critical gate whose scope the incident's consequence fell within (a relevant gate). One gate per row.
Gate criteria relied on for the judgement. Required for PASS and FAIL.

Projected Gate Result at the reference date, applying the canonical gate-result definitions to the controls and criteria engaged by the incident. PASS on a relevant gate is a false-reassurance case. INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION is a protocol code, not a gate result.
Framework gap revealed by this row, if any.
allowed_values: NONE | G1_NO_CONTROL | G2_NO_CRITERION | G3_EVIDENCE_PROFILE | G4_GATE_MAPPING | G5_GATE_CRITERION | G6_THREAT_MODEL

definition: Required if and only if gap_type is not NONE: what is missing, in which artefact, and the proposed criterion, evidence item, mapping or scenario text.
Coder's confidence in this row's judgements given source detail.
Reasoning, mandatory evidence items relied on, source section references, factor-consolidation crosswalk (for example from CF-A02; CF-B01). Example rows must contain FICTIONAL.
